title: Product Listing & Search
prompt: Design an e-commerce search and product listing page with filters, sorting and deep links. Search/indexing and inventory computation already exist on the server. Explain initial rendering, browser navigation and races between filter requests. Draw the component/data-flow architecture, define state owners and contracts, and explain performance, accessibility and recovery. No UI coding is required.
functionalReqs: Share and restore query, filters, sort and page through the URL
Render initial useful content and progressively hydrate controls
Show facet counts, empty results, skeletons and recoverable errors
nonFunctionalReqs: 40 products per page on a mobile network; prioritize one initial route and visible images, defer optional recommendation code.
Label filter groups, expose selected filters and clear-all, announce result count without stealing focus; use semantic product links and accessible mobile filter dialog focus restoration.
Abort and key-check responses; keep the previous grid visibly marked as updating. Back/forward restores the same committed URL state.

scale.notes: 40 products per page on a mobile network; prioritize one initial route and visible images, defer optional recommendation code.
scale.storage: 40 products with 100 KB thumbnails vs 20 KB responsive thumbnails; illustrative interview assumptions, not measured guarantees.

outOfScope: Backend sharding, ranking algorithms and infrastructure provisioning
Implementing a production UI inside this exercise
deepDives: The router owns committed URL state and SSRs the initial page for discovery. Client transitions cancel superseded requests and commit only a result matching the canonical query key. Reserve image dimensions and prioritize above-fold assets.
Rapid filter changes render results for the previous URL
CSR can be enough for an internal authenticated catalog. SSR improves initial discoverability but adds hydration and personalized-cache boundaries.
